title: Hybrid reranker 'surgeon' selection matrix and smoke/regression harness for multilingual traffic
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Our reranking endpoint has to serve mixed traffic from EN, ES, FR, JA, and other locales. Current experiments show good quality for a single large cross-encoder in English but variable latency and quality for other locales. We need a pragmatic selection strategy that mixes heavyweight cross-encoders for high-quality locales and lightweight quantized fallbacks where latency or cost constraints require it.

Goal: Define and implement a "surgeon" selection matrix (a deterministic policy that picks the smallest model that meets locale-specific quality & latency budgets), instrumented with a smoke/regression harness to detect quality regressions and latency SLO breaches during rollouts. This ticket covers design, initial implementation, and a staged canary rollout on internal traffic.

Success metrics (primary):
- P50 latency for rerank endpoint <= 40ms for heavyweight models; lightweight fallbacks P50 <= 18ms.
- P95 latency not to exceed 120ms for heavyweight, 60ms for lightweight.
- End-to-end rerank quality delta vs baseline cross-encoder: mean NDCG drop <= 0.01 for locales that use light fallback; keep >+0.02 lift for locales assigned heavy models.
- Regression alert triggering rate < 1 per week per locale during rollout.

Approach and scope:
1) Selection matrix: build a static configuration mapping locale -> prioritized candidate list (heavy-full, medium-quantized, lightweight distilled). Each candidate will include metadata: expected token budget, sequence-length profile, quantization tag, and cost multiplier. The matrix supports percent-splits for staged canaries.
2) "Surgeon" policy engine: a small runtime module that evaluates request context (locale header, max desired latency, cost tier) and selects the highest-quality candidate that fits the latency/cost budget. Engine will export selection reasons for observability (e.g., "picked quantized-4 for JA due to p95-budget breach").
3) Smoke & regression harness: extend the rerank regression suite with locale-aware synthetic prompt sets, a small human-in-the-loop sampling pipeline, and an automated A/B comparator that computes NDCG, MRR, and focused pairwise disagreements. Harness will run locally in CI and continuously in staging.
4) Canary rollout plan: 1% internal traffic -> 5% internal -> 10% internal -> 10% external pilot (selected customers) with gated progression based on quality & latency gates. Automatic rollback on sustained regression or SLO breach.
5) Monitoring & dashboards: per-locale KPIs (latency buckets, cost-per-call, NDCG vs baseline), plus a regression watchtower that calls out urgent drifts.

Trade-offs considered:
- Deterministic selection matrix simplifies debugging but sacrifices adaptive runtime learning; we plan follow-up to collect telemetry and iterate policy rules.
- Using quantized medium models reduces cost but requires extra regen checks for corner-case hallucination shifts.
- Human sampling for quality is slow; we rely on a hybrid strategy: automated metrics first, humans only when automated signals cross thresholds.

Implementation notes:
- Config format: top-level CSV/JSON row per locale for initial rollout (keeps deploy simple), later migrate to dynamic store.
- Engine will be added to the rerank request path as a fast filter; selection metadata will be written to trace headers and logs.
- Add a lightweight client-side SDK flag to override selection for tests.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RER/Surgeon+Selection+Matrix+Design
- Initial PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/1423
- Staging dashboard (early mock): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rerank/surgeon-selection-metrics

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Locale quality unknown for tiny distilled models -> mitigation: conservative default to heavy model for any locale with < 10K evaluation examples; require manual opt-in.
- Risk: Latency regression from selection logic -> mitigation: enable a fast-path cache for repeated prefix requests and add local circuit-breaker with fallback to previously-known-good model.

Next milestones:
- 2026-03-18: Merge prototype PR and smoke harness into staging (assigned Marco).
- 2026-03-25: Run 1% internal canary and collect 7-day metrics.
- 2026-04-08: External pilot with 2 partner customers if internal signals stable.

Notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on selection, initial harness, and rollout orchestration. Production-grade autoscaling of multiple model pools is tracked separately (see ENG-73401).
acceptance_criteria: Selection matrix exists and is deployed to staging as config file
Surgeon policy returns deterministic model choice and reason string on each rerank call
Smoke harness runs nightly in staging and publishes NDCG/MRR deltas per locale
Canary progression automation halts on quality or latency gate breaches
Tracing shows selection decisions and model variant identifiers for 100% of rerank calls in staging
